function: Beamspace channel estimation from few pilot observations (sparse reconstruction) with a deep-unfolded trimmed-ridge regression network and a model ensemble (p. 1, p. 7).
system: TDD mmWave massive MIMO, lens-array BS with N=256 antennas, 16 RF chains, 16 single-antenna users; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 2, p. 9).
method: Deep unfolding of iterative trimmed-ridge regression (30 layers, trainable A, rho, alpha), supervised MSE training offline; model-averaging ensemble of four models with different top-K (p. 7, p. 9).
data_channel: Own simulated Saleh-Valenzuela channels converted to beamspace by DFT; 80,000 training, 2,000 validation, 2,000 test samples; Bernoulli measurement matrix, Gaussian noise (p. 9).
test_conditions: Same simulated distribution for training and testing (held-out samples); SNR sweep -10 to 30 dB; M=128 and M=64 pilot-length models; no new scenario (p. 9, p. 10).
baselines: Non-learned: OMP, AMP, own iterative ITRR; learned: GM-LAMP, CNN-based network, SBL-CE-Net (p. 9).
metrics: Channel estimation NMSE; downlink sum rate with zero-forcing precoder; accurate-reconstruction ratio; training time (p. 9, p. 10, p. 11).
complexity: Order: ITRR O(TMN^2), UTRR forward pass O(LMN^2), sorting O(N logK); trainable parameters L(2MN+2); training time 255 min with CCR vs 548 min (p. 7, p. 10, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "we first use the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model in (2) to generate the spatial channel samples". Custom Saleh-Valenzuela simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "The training dataset, validation dataset and testing dataset contain" 80,000, 2,000 and 2,000 beamspace channels (held-out part of the same simulated data). p. 10 reports models for M = 64, but the weights have size M x 2N (p. 7), and the paper never tests a trained model in a new condition.
q3_support: p. 9: "OMP [18] and AMP [25] algorithms, and three deep-learning methods including a model-based network GM-LAMP [45], a model-free CNN-based network [33] and a sparse Bayesian learning unfolding network SBL-CE-Net [26]". p. 11: "the proposed UTRR-E achieved lower NMSEs for the entire SNR range".
q4_support: p. 12: "The forward-pass computational complexity of a UTRR network is O(LM N 2 )", with the order for ITRR, GM-LAMP, CNN, OMP and SBL-CE-Net also given.
q5_support: p. 9: "we first use the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model in (2) to generate the spatial channel samples". Data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Deep unfolding with trained parameters counts as learned. Area 2 because the learned method reconstructs the beamspace channel. Table I (p. 10) reports training time only; the complexity order that meets q4 is in Section V-G on p. 12.
